# visualize — pick the form the knowledge asks for

Render something already settled so it lands for someone else. The sibling of `frame-analogize`:
same direction (delivered to an audience, not derived for yourself), same premise (the thing is
understood; only its legibility is in question), different medium — a picture instead of a
comparison.

## Stance

- **Form follows the kind of knowledge, not the mood.** The table below is the whole instrument.
  Choosing a diagram because diagrams look thorough is how empty artifacts get made.
- **Terminal first; escalate on a real threshold.** A terminal drawing (ASCII flow, sequence,
  state, data-flow) is the default. Escalate to an interactive artifact only when **interaction
  changes visible state**, or the audience explicitly asks. "It would look nicer" is not a
  threshold.
- **The payload is never behind the interaction.** Anything that overturns what the audience
  currently believes must be legible without clicking. Progressive disclosure may fold detail; it
  may not fold the headline.
- **Name things by what the audience does with them.** Not by architectural category. Category
  words — *embedded · library · service · middleware · layer · mechanism · runtime · abstraction*,
  in any language — explain a shape to someone who already owns the taxonomy and say nothing to
  anyone else. Cash them out: an install line, an import, a call, a path, a command.
- **One example threads the whole thing**, starting where it is first exercised — small enough to
  be boring, rich enough to need the mechanism you are explaining.

## The grammar

| Kind of knowledge | Form | What makes it work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Ownership / boundary** — who holds what, where the lines are | **Spatial map** | Positions are permanent: a later, deeper view reuses the same layout one zoom in, so spatial memory keeps paying. |
| **Temporal process** — what happens in what order | **Run playback** | One example stepped line by line; an actor legend lighting per line; an annotation carrying the *why* of that line; a variant switch replaying the same example the other way. Watching one run beats mapping all runs for an audience with no model yet. |
| **State over time** — what accumulates, what expires | **Time stepper** | The stores side by side, advanced one event at a time. Expiry has to be *seen* leaving; a table can state a lifetime but cannot show one. |
| **Delta from what they know** | **Claim expansion** | Their own sentences as the rows, a verdict chip as the door, a fixed unfold behind each: mechanism → the trade-off → what it costs them. Correct claims expand too — a right answer is where the next layer is cheapest to add. |
| **Taxonomy** — families and members | **Grouped map** | Draw the grouping, not a literal tree: a slim header rather than a root floating beside a tall column, members in a strict N-column grid (free-wrapping produces orphan full-width cards). |
| **Structure / dependency** | **Weighted node-edge graph** | Arrows for who uses whom, **edge weights** marking the one canonical path, and every node's detail ending in clickable *next-step* hints. Without weights and a suggested walk it is an inventory, not a tour. |
| **Lifecycle / outcome classes** | **Canonical-run diagram** | A fixed spine, outcome selectors, a branch card dropping from the spine, and a terminal strip that distinguishes *loops back* from *finishes*. |

Composition is normal: a guided container (chapters, one takeaway each) holding several of these,
each chapter picking its own form. The container is not itself a form — it is the curriculum.

## Delivery discipline

- **Verify before delivering**: exercise every interaction, console clean, no horizontal overflow.
  Then, if you revised a page they already had open, **tell them to reload** — a local file does
  not refresh itself, and a stale tab has been mistaken for a broken build.
- **Labels render in the audience's language**; the names in this file are roles, not strings.
- **Self-contained**: no external requests; inline everything.
- **Responsive**: rearrange stages rather than shrinking the whole drawing.
- **CSS trap worth knowing**: an author `display:` rule beats the UA `[hidden]` rule — pair any
  `display:flex/grid` class with `.cls[hidden]{display:none}` if you toggle visibility by attribute.
- **Delegating the build?** Copy these rules into the brief. A worker sees only the brief.

## The paid lessons (verbatim, still binding)

> Making every box clickable did not make the model easier to understand: each click merely
> replaced one block of prose with another.

> A mechanically correct interaction can still be pedagogically empty when the visible system
> itself does not change.

## Companion skills

- **`frame-analogize`** — the same delivery direction through a stress-tested analogy; reach for
  it when the difficulty is conceptual rather than structural.
- **`shape-mockup`** — renders disposable candidates so a decision can be **picked**; here the
  artifact **is** the explanation and nothing is being chosen.
- **`fathom-guide`** — borrows this grammar by protocol when teaching a repository level, and
  adds its own pedagogical overlays (gloss layer, per-level defaults, the correction rule).

## Communication style

Explain in the audience's language with simple, direct wording. Lead with one plain sentence; put
precision after, only where needed; keep code, identifiers, and paths in their original form.
